finding.claim: /transfer does not validate that amount is positive. A negative amount passes the balance check (BAL[user] < negative is False), then debits the sender by a negative value (credit) and debits the recipient. The attacker steals funds from any account and can mint unlimited balance. Non-numeric amounts or unknown recipients also cause 500s. The check-then-update is also non-atomic (race condition).
finding.source: request.json['amount'] and request.json['to'] from an authenticated POST body

trace.note: to taken from request JSON, unvalidated
amount taken from request JSON, no type or sign check
only checks BAL[g.user] < amount; passes for negative amount
victim balance decreases by |amount| (BAL[to] may go negative)

finding.guards_checked: Compared with /withdraw, which has an amount <= 0 check at line 21; /transfer has no equivalent. No other validation, no lock around the check and update, and no check that 'to' differs from the sender. Authentication that sets g.user is not present in this file.

verdict.guard_found: none (only the BAL[g.user] < amount balance check at bank.py:11, which a negative amount passes; /withdraw has an amount <= 0 check at line 21 but /transfer does not)
verdict.reason: bank.py:11 only tests BAL[g.user] < amount, so a negative amount passes, and bank.py:13-14 then credit the sender and debit the recipient. Any authenticated user can send this request, and the file has no positivity check, lock or type validation.
